items.title: The public law overhang in arbitration: Does the public sector trigger differential judicial oversight?
items.summary: On paper, India appears arbitration-friendly. The Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, based on the UNCITRAL Model Law, was enacted to make arbitration a final, efficient and autonomous method of commercial dispute resolution, subject to narrowly circumscribed judicial supervision. Over 3 decades, the Supreme Court repeatedly affirmed party autonomy, finality of awards and limited judicial intervention. Yet, a second, less predictable line of decisions has emerged. These decisions commonly involve large public infrastructure projects, substantial claims against the State or State-owned entities and judicial interventions that would be surprising in purely private commercial disputes. This article argues that the tension is institutional rather than doctrinal: constitutional courts in India, accustomed to supervising public administration and protecting the public exchequer, sometimes carry public law instincts into commercial adjudication when the State is a party. The result is not an explicit re-writing of arbitration law, but a gradual shift in how courts apply its limits. items.title: Prajwal Revanna sent to police custody for two days over mobile phone use in prison
items.summary: A Bengaluru court on Tuesday sent former MP Prajwal Revanna to police custody for two days in connection with the alleged use of mobile phone inside Parappana Agrahara Central Prison where he lodged for rape case. Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Sandeep Patil passed the order after hearing the prosecution and defence. Sandeep Patil Prajwal Revanna, who represented the Hassan parliamentary constituency from 2019 to 2023, is serving life sentence after being convicted of rape in August 2025. The present case stemmed from a raid conducted by Central Crime Branch (CCB) which allegedly led to recovery of mobile phones and other digital devices from Revanna. According to the complaint, the CCB recovered a Redmi 5G smartphone, a blue packet notebook, a charger and a SanDisk pen drive from a high-security barrack during a raid conducted on August 11. Revanna allegedly claimed that the notebook belonged to him. The police claimed that they found Facebook, WhatsApp, Instagram, Netflix, Prime Video and other applications installed on the smartphone. items.title: Sikkim district judge moves Supreme Court against High Court, alleges vindictive vigilance action
items.summary: A sitting district judge in Sikkim has approached the Supreme Court against the Sikkim High Court, alleging that he has been subjected to a sustained campaign of harassment and retaliatory vigilance action after he complained against a then sitting judge of the High Court, who is now retired. District and Sessions Judge at Mangan, Prajwal Khatiwada , has filed a writ petition under Article 32 challenging a show cause notice issued to him by the High Court of Sikkim on August 12. The petition names the High Court of Sikkim, its Registrar (Vigilance), Vigilance Inspector Sarad Subba and the State of Sikkim as respondents. Khatiwada joined the Sikkim Judicial Service in 2005 after topping the State's judicial service examination. He served as Registrar General of the High Court from February 2023 to December 2025 before being posted to Mangan. According to the petition, the trouble started after Khatiwada lodged a formal complaint on December 12, 2025 against a then sitting judge of the High Court, alleging mistreatment and humiliation.
